chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Murram from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who gives some of his wealth to a man during his illness, he said: 'If he revokes it, it is valid.'

key_terms.أَبَانَهُ: he revoked it / made it clear he took it back
key_terms.مَرَضِهِ: illness (specifically referring to the state of illness during which a gift is given)

ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke a gift given during their illness?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a gift given during illness is revocable unless specified otherwise, distinguishing it from the final bequest (wasiyyah) which is binding after death. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for determining whether property transferred during the 'hour of death' is treated as a gift or part of the estate, impacting inheritance calculations. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Tusi school's reporting through Ibn Abi Umayr and Muramiz.
